definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{NP}}
definitions.construction:
\[\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)=\bigl\{P:\text{conditions (i)--(iv) below hold}\bigr\}.\]
Condition \(\mathrm{(i)}\): for every \(n\), \((Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independently and identically distributed under \(P\) in \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(ii)}\): \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on its compact support \(\mathcal X_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), with \(L^{-1}\leq\inf_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}f_P(x)\leq L\), and \(\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a rectifiable curve.  Condition \(\mathrm{(iii)}\): \(\mu_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x]\) belongs to \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\).  Condition \(\mathrm{(iv)}\): \(\sigma_P^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x)\) is continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\) and satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma_P^2(x)\leq L\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).

definitions.name: \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{NP}}_n
definitions.construction:
\[
 \mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}
 =\left\{\widehat\mu_n:\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there is one measurable map }T_n:(\mathbb R\times[0,\infty))^n\to\mathbb R
 \text{ selected independently of }P,\\
 \widehat\mu_n(x)=T_n(V_{n,P}(x))
 \text{ for every }x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{T}^{\mathrm{PI}}_n
definitions.construction:
\[
 \mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}
 =\left\{\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{PI}}:\begin{array}{l}
 \text{there is a family }\{T_{n,x}:x\in\mathbb R^2\}\text{ selected independently of }P,\\
 T_{n,x}:(\mathbb R\times[0,\infty))^n\to\mathbb R
 \text{ is Borel measurable for every fixed }x,\\
 \widehat\mu_{n,P}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)=T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))
 \text{ for every }P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\\
 \text{and every }x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)
 \end{array}\right\}.
\]
No joint measurability, continuity, common modulus, or other regularity of \(x\mapsto T_{n,x}\) is required.

definitions.name: R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}
definitions.construction:
For an extended nonnegative function \(Z\) on the sample space, define its outer expectation by
\[
 \mathbb E_P^*[Z]
 =\inf\left\{\mathbb E_P[W]:
 W\text{ is an extended nonnegative measurable function and }W\geq Z
 \text{ pointwise}\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}
 =\inf_{\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}
 \left|\widehat\mu_{n,P}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)-\mu_P(x)\right|
 \right].
\]

definitions.name: K_\square
definitions.construction:
Define the fixed uniform kernel by
\[
 K_\square(u)=\mathbf 1\{|u|\leq1\},\qquad u\in\mathbb R.
\]

definitions.name: G_P
definitions.construction:
For a member law \(P\), the known design object is
\[
 G_P=(\mathcal X_P,\mathcal A_{0,P},\mathcal A_{1,P},\mathcal B_P,d_P,K_\square),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_{0,P}\) and \(\mathcal A_{1,P}\) are a Borel partition of \(\mathcal X_P\), \(\mathcal B_P=\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_{0,P})\cap\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_{1,P})\subset\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X_P)\), and the fixed metric is \(d_P(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\).

definitions.name: U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)
definitions.construction:
For \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), define
\[
 D^{\pm}_{P,x}=\{\mathbf 1(X\in\mathcal A_{1,P})-\mathbf 1(X\in\mathcal A_{0,P})\}\lVert X-x\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n).
\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{12}
definitions.construction:
For integers \(p\geq1\), real numbers \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\), let \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) be the set of laws \(P\) satisfying all the following member properties.

\(\mathrm{(i)}\) For every \(n\), the vectors \((Y_i(0),Y_i(1),X_i)\), \(1\leq i\leq n\), are independently and identically distributed; \(T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_{1,P}\}\); and \(Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0)\).

\(\mathrm{(ii)}\) The support has the CTY rectangular form \(\mathcal X_P=[\underline x_P,\overline x_P]^2\subseteq[-L,L]^2\).  The variable \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\), such that \(L^{-1}\leq f_P(x)\leq L\) for all \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).

\(\mathrm{(iii)}\) For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(\mu_{t,P}(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=x]\) has a \(C^{p+1}\) extension to an open neighborhood of \(\mathcal X_P\), and
\[
 \max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}|\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)|
 +\max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\neq z\in\mathcal X_P}
 { |\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)-\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(z)|\over\lVert x-z\rVert_2}
 \leq L.
\]

\(\mathrm{(iv)}\) For each \(t\), \(\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(t)\mid X=x)\) is continuous and satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)\leq L\) on \(\mathcal X_P\).

\(\mathrm{(v)}\) For each \(t\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|^{2+\nu}\mid X=x]\leq L.
\]

\(\mathrm{(vi)}\) The sets \(\mathcal A_{0,P}\) and \(\mathcal A_{1,P}\) form a Borel partition of \(\mathcal X_P\), and their known common interface \(\mathcal B_P\subset\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a compact rectifiable curve satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\leq L\).

\(\mathrm{(vii)}\) The known metric is exactly Euclidean, \(d_P(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2\), and the known kernel is \(K_\square\).  The collection
\[
 \{\{z\in\mathcal X_P:\lVert z-x\rVert_2\leq r\}:x\in\mathcal X_P, r\geq0\}
\]
is a VC class with VC index at most four.

\(\mathrm{(viii)}\) Put \(r_p(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(I_1=[0,\infty)\), \(I_0=(-\infty,0)\), and
\[
 \Psi_{t,P,x}(h)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[
 {1\over h^2}\mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)^\top
 \right].
\]
For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\Psi_{t,P,x}(h))\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\(\mathrm{(ix)}\) For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\),
\[
 {1\over h^2}\int_{\mathcal A_{t,P}}
 K_\square(\{(2t-1)\lVert z-x\rVert_2\}/h)\,dz\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\(\mathrm{(x)}\) For every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), both \(t\), and every \(0<s\leq L^{-1}\), the one-dimensional Hausdorff integral of \(f_P\) over
\[
 \{z\in\mathcal A_{t,P}:\lVert z-x\rVert_2=s\}
\]
is finite and strictly positive.

These clauses are the exact \(L\)-uniformized conditions from CTY Assumptions~1--2 and Theorem~2 used below.  In particular, clause \(\mathrm{(v)}\) is the raw conditional-moment envelope, and clause \(\mathrm{(vii)}\) retains the uniform-kernel VC requirement in Assumption~2(iii).

definitions.name: \mathcal{T}^{12,\pm}_n
definitions.construction:
Let \(\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n\) be the class of rules for which there is one collection
\[
 \{T_{n,G,x}:G\text{ is an admissible known geometry},\ x\in\mathbb R^2\}
\]
selected independently of the unknown member law, such that every fixed \((G,x)\) section is a Borel map from \((\mathbb R\times\mathbb R)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\) and
\[
 \widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)=T_{n,G_P,x}(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)),
 \qquad P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L),\quad x\in\mathcal B_P.
\]
No joint measurability, continuity, common modulus, or other regularity in \(x\) is imposed.

definitions.name: R_n^{12,\pm}
definitions.construction:
For an extended nonnegative function \(Z\), put
\[
 \mathbb E_P^*[Z]=\inf\{\mathbb E_P[W]:W\text{ is extended nonnegative and measurable, and }W\geq Z\text{ pointwise}\}.
\]
Define
\[
 R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)=
 \inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right].
\]

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}
definitions.construction:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(h>0\), let
\[
 \widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)={1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and
\[
 \widehat m_{t,x}(h)={1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)Y_i.
\]
If \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h))\geq(2L)^{-1}\), set
\(\widehat\beta_{t,x}(h)=\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)^{-1}\widehat m_{t,x}(h)\); otherwise set \(\widehat\beta_{t,x}(h)=0\).  With \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), define
\[
 \widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)=
 \Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\!\left\{e_1^\top(\widehat\beta_{1,x}(h)-\widehat\beta_{0,x}(h))\right\}.
\]
Here \(\Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\) is Euclidean projection.  This rule is a fixed, law-independent, jointly Borel member of \(\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n\).

definitions.name: b_{n,\nu}
definitions.construction:
Let
\[
 b_{n,\nu}=a_n+\left\{{\log n\over n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}}\right\}^{1/3},
 \qquad a_n=\left({\log n\over n}\right)^{1/4}.
\]

statements.statement:
Let all spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) be standard Borel.  Let \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) be independent uniform binary variables.  Conditionally on them, let \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) be independent, with the law of \(Z_j\) depending only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and with the law of \(Z_0\) independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).  Suppose decoder \(j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), where \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), and write \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\) and \(\rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).  Then every such decentralized decoder obeys
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one decoding error}\}
 \geq\frac12\left[1-\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}\right].
\]
Along any sequence with \(M=M_n\to\infty\) and fixed \(\kappa<1\), this lower bound is \(1/2-o(1)\).
statements.justification: The finite-\(M\) overlap decomposition gives the exact simultaneous-error certificate \(\frac12[1-\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}]\); its asymptotic \(1/2-o(1)\) consequence is invoked only after the packing verifies \(M=M_n\to\infty\).
statements.gap: The lemma allows a different measurable decoder at every coordinate and therefore supplies the multiple-coordinate step needed for arbitrary point-indexed sections.
statements.consumer: The point-indexed converse applies the lemma with \(M=M_n\) and \(\kappa=2\alpha<1\).
statements.proof_tex:
For each \(j\), dominate \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) by \(Q_{j,0}+Q_{j,1}\), and write the resulting densities as \(q_{j,0}\) and \(q_{j,1}\).  The common subprobability measure has density \(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1}\) and mass
\[
 \rho_j=\int(q_{j,0}\wedge q_{j,1})
 =1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
Construct an equivalent version of the experiment as follows.  Independently across coordinates, draw an ambiguity indicator \(A_j\), independent of \(\Omega_j\), with \(\Pr(A_j=1)=\rho_j\).  On \(\{A_j=1\}\), draw \(S_j\) from the normalized common submeasure, independently of \(\Omega_j\).  On \(\{A_j=0\}\), draw \(S_j\) from the normalized residual measure belonging to \(\Omega_j\).  When a normalizing mass is zero, assign an arbitrary probability kernel to the corresponding probability-zero branch.  The resulting conditional law of \(S_j\) given \(\Omega_j=b\) is exactly \(Q_{j,b}\).

Because the spaces are standard Borel and \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), a regular conditional distribution of \(Z_j\) given \((S_j,\Omega_j)\) exists.  Sampling from those kernels reconstructs the prescribed conditional law of every \(Z_j\), and sampling \(Z_0\) independently from its bit-independent law reconstructs the joint experiment by the assumed conditional product structure.  Standard-Borel kernel randomization permits all these draws to be realized using latent uniforms independent of the bits.

Condition on the ambiguity indicators, all latent randomization other than the bits, and all bits outside
\[
 \mathcal A=\{j:A_j=1\}.
\]
Suppose \(\mathcal A\neq\varnothing\).  The bit configurations on \(\mathcal A\) for which all decoders are correct form an independent set in the \(|\mathcal A|\)-dimensional binary hypercube.  Indeed, take two configurations differing only in coordinate \(j\in\mathcal A\).  The decoder for coordinate \(j\) receives the same \(S_j\), because the common-submeasure branch is independent of \(\Omega_j\); it also receives the same \(Z_{-j}\) and \(Z_0\), because every other bit and all latent randomization are fixed.  Its input is therefore identical although the correct value of \(\Omega_j\) is reversed, so the decoder cannot be correct at both endpoints of that hypercube edge.  Pairing vertices along any fixed coordinate shows that an independent set has at most \(2^{|\mathcal A|-1}\) vertices.  The ambiguous bits remain independent and uniform under the conditioning.  Hence the conditional probability of simultaneous success is at most \(1/2\) on \(\{\mathcal A\neq\varnothing\}\), while it is at most one on \(\{\mathcal A=\varnothing\}\).  Averaging and using independence of the \(A_j\)'s gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 &\leq \Pr(\mathcal A=\varnothing)+\frac12\Pr(\mathcal A\neq\varnothing)\\
 &=\frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to derive the finite-\(M\) relative-entropy consequence.  Let
\[
 H_j=\int\sqrt{q_{j,0}q_{j,1}}
\]
be the Hellinger affinity.  Jensen's inequality under \(Q_{j,0}\) yields
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\geq-2\log H_j.
\]
The elementary affinity bound for total variation follows from Cauchy--Schwarz:
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
 &=\frac12\int|\sqrt{q_{j,0}}-\sqrt{q_{j,1}}|
             (\sqrt{q_{j,0}}+\sqrt{q_{j,1}})\\
 &\leq\sqrt{1-H_j^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \rho_j
 \geq1-\sqrt{1-e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})}}
 \geq\frac12e^{-\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})},
\]
where the last inequality uses \(1-\sqrt{1-u}=u/(1+\sqrt{1-u})\geq u/2\) for \(0\leq u\leq1\).  Under the asserted entropy bound,
\[
 \rho_j\geq\frac12M^{-\kappa}.
\]
Therefore \(1-v\leq e^{-v}\) gives the finite-\(M\) estimate
\[
 \prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)
 \leq\exp\!\left\{-\sum_{j=1}^M\rho_j\right\}
 \leq\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}.
\]
Subtracting the simultaneous-success bound from one proves
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one decoding error}\}
 \geq\frac12\left[1-\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}\right].
\]
If \(M=M_n\to\infty\) and \(\kappa<1\) is fixed, then \(M_n^{1-\kappa}\to\infty\), so the exponential term is \(o(1)\), which proves the final assertion.

statements.statement:
For every \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\), there are constants \(c_0,c_1>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1/8\), depending only on \(q\) and \(L\), such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), there exist \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\) points \(x_1,\ldots,x_{M_n}\) on the boundary of the square \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), separated by at least a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\), a radius \(w_n\asymp a_n^{1/q}\), and laws \(P_\omega\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), indexed by \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), with the following properties.  Every law has support \(S\), a continuous density \(f_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq f_{P_\omega}\leq L\), a regression \(\mu_{P_\omega}\) in the stated \(q\)-H\"older ball, and a continuous conditional variance \(\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\) satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{P_\omega}\leq L\).  The boundary \(\operatorname{bd}(S)\) is rectifiable and the observations are independently and identically distributed.  The half-discs
\[
 C_j=B_2(x_j,w_n)\cap S,\qquad 1\leq j\leq M_n,
\]
are pairwise disjoint.  The subprobability law \(P_\omega\{(Y,X)\in\cdot,\ X\in C_j\}\) depends on \(\omega\) only through \(\omega_j\); the subprobability law \(P_\omega\{(Y,X)\in\cdot,\ X\in S\setminus\bigcup_{k=1}^{M_n}C_k\}\) is independent of \(\omega\); and \(P_\omega(X\in C_j)=m_n\) for one common number \(m_n\) independent of \(j\) and \(\omega\).  There are numbers \(u_{j,0},u_{j,1}\) such that
\[
 \mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)=u_{j,\omega_j},
 \qquad |u_{j,1}-u_{j,0}|\geq c_1a_n.
\]
If \(\omega^{(j)}\) differs from \(\omega\) only in coordinate \(j\), then the laws of \(\lVert X-x_j\rVert_2\) agree, the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside radii of order \(a_n\), and
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(\mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}\right)
 \leq\alpha\log M_n.
\]
statements.justification: The construction is the same-class witness: it places separated boundary alternatives in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) and proves cellwise locality, value separation, common cell mass, and the compressed Kullback--Leibler bound.
statements.gap: Its role is confined to the explicit square-support finite submodel; the outer-expectation minimax quantifiers and sectionwise estimator class are handled in the converse theorem.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite hypercube and local divergence bound used by the point-indexed theorem and, through inclusion, by the CTY corollary.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), and place all centers on a fixed middle subinterval of the lower edge of \(S\).  If \(x_j\) is such a center, then, for every sufficiently small \(r>0\), the part of the circle of radius \(r\) lying in \(S\) is
\[
 x_j+r e_\theta,
 \qquad e_\theta=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta),
 \qquad 0\leq\theta\leq\pi.
\]
The construction uses the elementary identities
\[
 \int_0^\pi\cos\theta\,d\theta=0,
 \qquad
 \int_0^\pi\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac\pi2.
\]

Choose \(\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))\) with \(0\leq\psi\leq1\) and \(\psi(0)=1\), and set
\[
 \phi(z)=\psi(\lVert z\rVert_2^2),
 \qquad
 \varphi(u)=\psi(u^2).
\]
For constants \(d,d_1>0\), to be chosen below, define
\[
 \Delta=d a_n,
 \qquad
 w=(d_1\Delta)^{1/q}.
\]
Choose a maximal grid of centers on the indicated middle subinterval with separation \(3w\).  For all sufficiently large \(n\), the half-discs
\[
 C_j=B_2(x_j,w)\cap S
\]
are pairwise disjoint and avoid the corners.  Elementary interval packing gives
\[
 M_n\asymp w^{-1},
 \qquad
 M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q},
\]
where all constants may depend only on \(q\) and \(L\).  Thus \(w_n=w\asymp a_n^{1/q}\), and the separation is a constant multiple of \(a_n^{1/q}\).  Write \(r_j(z)=\lVert z-x_j\rVert_2\) and \(\phi_j(z)=\phi((z-x_j)/w)\).

Fix a sufficiently small slope \(b>0\).  For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), define
\[
 p_\omega(z)=\frac12+bz_1+\Delta\sum_{j=1}^{M_n}\omega_j\phi_j(z).
\]
For every integer \(0\leq k\leq q\), scaling gives
\[
 \lVert D^k(\Delta\phi_j)\rVert_\infty
 \leq C_{\phi,q}\Delta w^{-k}.
\]
For \(k=q\), the right-hand side is \(C_{\phi,q}/d_1\); for \(k<q\), it converges to zero.  The supports are disjoint, so summation does not enlarge these suprema.  Choose \(b\) small, next \(d_1\) large, and finally \(d\) small.  The affine part and scaled bumps then put every \(p_\omega\) in \(\mathcal H^q(S,L)\), and, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \frac14\leq p_\omega(z)\leq\frac34.
\]

Let \(\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) satisfy \(0\leq\chi\leq1\), \(\chi(v)=0\) for \(v\leq1\), and \(\chi(v)=1\) for \(v\geq2\).  Fix \(c_A\geq8\), increasing \(d_1\) if necessary so that \(2c_A\Delta/b<w\) eventually, including when \(q=1\), and define
\[
 A_n(r)=-\frac{2\Delta\varphi(r/w)}{br}
 \chi\!\left(\frac{br}{c_A\Delta}\right),
 \qquad A_n(0)=0.
\]
The cutoff makes \(A_n\) identically zero in a neighborhood of zero, while compact support of \(\varphi(r/w)\) makes it vanish smoothly before \(r=w\).  On the region where it can be nonzero, \(br>c_A\Delta\), and hence
\[
 |A_n(r)|\leq\frac{2}{c_A}\leq\frac14.
\]
Define on \(S\)
\[
 f_\omega(z)=1+
 \sum_{j=1}^{M_n}\omega_j A_n(r_j(z))
 \frac{z_1-(x_j)_1}{r_j(z)}\mathbf 1\{r_j(z)<w\},
\]
with each summand defined to be zero at its center.  Disjointness makes the formula unambiguous.  The two cutoff properties show that \(f_\omega\) is continuous on \(S\), and
\[
 \frac34\leq f_\omega(z)\leq\frac54.
\]
For each affected half-disc, polar integration gives
\[
 \int_0^w A_n(r)r\,dr\int_0^\pi\cos\theta\,d\theta=0.
\]
Therefore \(\int_S f_\omega(z)\,dz=1\).  Positivity makes \(S\) the support.  Since \(L\geq4\), the displayed density interval is contained in \([L^{-1},L]\), and \(S\subset[-L,L]^2\) is compact with rectifiable boundary.

Conditional on \(X=z\), let
\[
 Y=B+\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 B\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_\omega(z)),
 \qquad
 \varepsilon\sim N(0,1),
\]
where \(B\) and \(\varepsilon\) are conditionally independent.  Then
\[
 \mu_{P_\omega}(z)=p_\omega(z),
 \qquad
 \sigma_{P_\omega}^2(z)=1+p_\omega(z)\{1-p_\omega(z)\}.
\]
The variance is continuous and belongs to \([1,5/4]\subseteq[L^{-1},L]\).  Draw the \(n\) observations independently from this common law.  Thus condition \(\mathrm{(i)}\) in \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) holds by construction; condition \(\mathrm{(ii)}\) follows from compactness, rectifiability, normalization, continuity, positivity, and the density envelope just verified; condition \(\mathrm{(iii)}\) is the scaled H\"older calculation; and condition \(\mathrm{(iv)}\) is the displayed variance calculation.  Hence every \(P_\omega\) belongs to the same class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).

We next record the cellwise locality properties.  Because the half-discs are disjoint, on \(C_j\) both \(p_\omega\) and \(f_\omega\), and hence the joint law of \((Y,X)\) restricted to \(X\in C_j\), depend on \(\omega\) only through \(\omega_j\).  Outside \(\bigcup_k C_k\), all bump and angular-density terms vanish, so the restricted joint law is independent of \(\omega\).  The zero angular integral above and congruence of the half-discs give, for every \(j\) and \(\omega\),
\[
 P_\omega(X\in C_j)=\int_{C_j}f_\omega(z)\,dz
 =|C_j|=\frac{\pi w^2}{2}=:m_n.
\]
Finally, disjointness and \(\phi_j(x_j)=1\) yield
\[
 \mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)=\frac12+b(x_j)_1+\Delta\omega_j
 =:u_{j,\omega_j},
 \qquad |u_{j,1}-u_{j,0}|=\Delta=d a_n.
\]
This proves the four cellwise assertions in the statement, including the boundary-value separation with \(c_1=d\).

It remains to establish the compressed-experiment properties.  Compare adjacent vertices, orienting the notation first so that \(\omega_j=1\) and \(\omega_j^{(j)}=0\).  All other perturbations vanish in \(C_j\).  At every \(0<r<w\), the angular density correction has integral zero, so the two radial densities agree and equal \(\pi r\).  For \(r\geq w\), the adjacent score densities are pointwise identical.  Thus the complete laws of \(\lVert X-x_j\rVert_2\) agree.

For \(0<r<w\), the difference of the outcome-weighted angular integrals is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\int_0^\pi p_\omega(x_j+re_\theta)
 \{1+A_n(r)\cos\theta\}\,d\theta
 -\int_0^\pi p_{\omega^{(j)}}(x_j+re_\theta)\,d\theta\\
 &\qquad=\pi\Delta\varphi(r/w)+\frac\pi2brA_n(r).
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, the constant part and the radial bump multiplied by \(A_n(r)\cos\theta\) integrate to zero, while the affine angular term gives the second cosine identity above.  If \(br\geq2c_A\Delta\), then \(\chi=1\) and the last display is zero.  For \(r\geq w\), both adjacent perturbations vanish.  Conditional on a radius, an angular mixture of Bernoulli variables is Bernoulli with the angularly averaged success probability, and convolution with the common Gaussian preserves equality.  Therefore versions of the conditional radial outcome laws agree outside
\[
 0\leq r<\frac{2c_A\Delta}{b},
\]
an interval whose length is of order \(a_n\).

On this exceptional interval the common radial density is bounded by \(Cr\), both averaged Bernoulli probabilities lie in \([1/4,3/4]\), and their difference is at most \(C\Delta\).  The inequality \(\log t\leq t-1\), applied to the two Bernoulli atoms, gives
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(p,p')
 \leq\frac{(p-p')^2}{p'(1-p')}
 \leq C\Delta^2.
\]
Applying the log-sum inequality after the common Gaussian Markov kernel shows that its output relative entropy is no larger.  Disintegration with respect to the common radial marginal consequently gives, for one compressed observation,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(P^{\mathrm{rad}}_{\omega,j},P^{\mathrm{rad}}_{\omega^{(j)},j})
 \leq C\Delta^2\int_0^{2c_A\Delta/b}r\,dr
 \leq C'\Delta^4.
\]
The argument is unchanged after reversing the adjacent orientation.  Factorization of the likelihood ratio for the independent product then gives
\[
 \operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}
 \right)
 \leq C'n\Delta^4=C'd^4\log n.
\]
Because the chosen maximal grid has \(M_n\asymp w^{-1}\),
\[
 \log M_n=\left(\frac{1}{4q}+o(1)\right)\log n.
\]
Choose \(d>0\) small enough that the preceding divergence is at most \(\alpha\log M_n\) for one fixed \(0<\alpha<1/8\), without disturbing any earlier envelope choice.  All asserted properties have now been verified.

statements.justification: The exact inherited CTY common-map statement follows from \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\geq R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\) and the point-indexed theorem.  For common Borel maps the boundary loss supremum is universally measurable, so ordinary completed expectation equals outer expectation.
statements.gap: No separate testing construction is needed for the common-map corollary once the stronger sectionwise-Borel theorem and the measurability bridge are established.
statements.consumer: This resolves the printed CTY logarithmic lower-bound conjecture on their inherited decision class in the stated regime \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(q\geq1\), and \(L\geq4\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\).  For a fixed \(n\geq2\), take any \(\widehat\mu_n\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}distance\text{-}decision\text{-}class}\), there is one law-independent Borel map
\[
 T_n:(\mathbb R\times[0,\infty))^n\longrightarrow\mathbb R
\]
such that \(\widehat\mu_n(x)=T_n(V_{n,P}(x))\) at every boundary point.  Equivalently, define the point-indexed family by \(T_{n,x}=T_n\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^2\).  Every fixed-\(x\) section is Borel and the family is law-independent.  This is the inclusion part of \(\mathrm{lem:common\text{-}map\text{-}strict\text{-}in\text{-}point\text{-}indexed}\), so
\[
 \mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\subseteq\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}.
\]

We next verify that the ordinary expectation in the Cattaneo--Titiunik--Yu risk agrees with the outer expectation used by the point-indexed risk.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), write a full sample point as \(\mathbf z=((y_i,\xi_i):1\leq i\leq n)\), and put
\[
 D_n(x,\mathbf z)=((y_i,\lVert\xi_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n),
 \qquad
 \ell_{P,n}(x,\mathbf z)
 =\left|T_n(D_n(x,\mathbf z))-\mu_P(x)\right|.
\]
The map \((x,\mathbf z)\mapsto D_n(x,\mathbf z)\) is Borel because each Euclidean-distance coordinate is continuous.  The map \(T_n\) is Borel by the decision-class definition, and \(\mu_P\) is continuous because it lies in \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\).  Hence \(\ell_{P,n}\) is jointly Borel on \(\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\times(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2)^n\).  The boundary is compact because \(\mathcal X_P\) is compact.  Consequently, for every real \(t\),
\[
 \left\{\mathbf z:
   \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}
   \ell_{P,n}(x,\mathbf z)>t
 \right\}
 =\operatorname{proj}_{\mathbf z}
 \left\{(x,\mathbf z):
   x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P),\ 
   \ell_{P,n}(x,\mathbf z)>t
 \right\}.
\]
The set on the right before projection is Borel in a product of standard Borel spaces, so its projection is analytic and therefore belongs to the completion of every probability measure on the sample space.  Thus the nonnegative boundary supremum is upper semianalytic, hence universally measurable.  A universally measurable nonnegative function has a measurable version under the completed product law, and the completed expectation of that version equals its outer expectation.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[
   \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}
   |\widehat\mu_n(x)-\mu_P(x)|
 \right]
 =
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
   \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}
   |\widehat\mu_n(x)-\mu_P(x)|
 \right].
\]
This argument uses joint measurability only for the common-map rule; it imposes no joint measurability on an arbitrary member of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\).

The two minimax risks use the same law class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).  The last equality and the inclusion of decision classes therefore give, for every \(n\geq2\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}
 &=\inf_{\widehat\mu_n\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}}
   \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)}
   \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
     \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}
     |\widehat\mu_n(x)-\mu_P(x)|
   \right]\\
 &\geq
   \inf_{\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}}
   \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)}
   \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
     \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}
     |\widehat\mu_{n,P}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)-\mu_P(x)|
   \right]
 =R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The sibling result \(\mathrm{thm:point\text{-}indexed\text{-}distance\text{-}log\text{-}converse}\) supplies a constant \(c_{\mathrm{PI}}(q,L)>0\) satisfying
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}}{a_n}
 \geq c_{\mathrm{PI}}(q,L).
\]
Monotonicity of \(\liminf\) and the preceding pointwise risk inequality yield
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}}{a_n}
 \geq c_{\mathrm{PI}}(q,L).
\]
Finally, \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) by \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rates}\), while \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) is exactly the infimum--supremum functional displayed in the theorem by \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}distance\text{-}risk}\).  Therefore the two displayed lower limits in the statement are equal.  Taking \(c_{\mathrm{CTY}}(q,L)=c_{\mathrm{PI}}(q,L)>0\) proves the claim.  Because no law class was changed in the comparison, this is a converse on the exact class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\); it neither invokes an Assumption~2 upper theorem nor asserts a matched two-sided frontier.

statements.justification: The reflection witness proves that allowing arbitrary Borel fixed sections genuinely enlarges the inherited one-common-map class, rather than merely reparameterizing it.
statements.gap: The witness requires no joint measurability: the family \(T_{n,x}(v)=x_1\) has Borel fixed sections, while equal reflected compressed laws rule out representation by one common map.
statements.consumer: It certifies the strict decision-class strengthening stated in the point-indexed headline and the inclusion used by the CTY corollary.
statements.proof_tex:
Take a rule in \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), generated by one law-independent Borel map
\[
 T_n:(\mathbb R\times[0,\infty))^n\longrightarrow\mathbb R.
\]
Set \(T_{n,x}=T_n\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^2\).  Each fixed section is Borel measurable, the entire family is selected independently of \(P\), and
\[
 T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))=T_n(V_{n,P}(x))
\]
at every boundary point.  Thus \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\subseteq\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\).  This inclusion uses only sectionwise measurability and imposes no joint condition in \(x\).

For strictness, consider the law-independent point-indexed family
\[
 T_{n,x}(v)=x_1,
 \qquad x=(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2.
\]
For every fixed \(x\), this is a constant, hence Borel measurable, function of \(v\).  It therefore defines a member of \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\).

Let \(P_0\) be the law under which \(X\) is uniform on \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\) and \(Y\sim N(0,1)\) is independent of \(X\).  Its density is one on its compact support, its boundary is rectifiable, its regression is zero, and its conditional variance is one.  Hence \(P_0\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) for every \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\).  At the boundary points
\[
 x_-=(-1/2,0),
 \qquad
 x_+=(1/2,0),
\]
reflection of the square in the vertical axis, together with independence of \(Y\), gives
\[
 \mathcal L_{P_0}\{V_{n,P_0}(x_-)\}
 =\mathcal L_{P_0}\{V_{n,P_0}(x_+)\}.
\]
If the displayed point-indexed family were generated by one common Borel map \(T_n\), applying that map to these identically distributed inputs would produce outputs with the same law.  The required outputs, however, are the distinct constants
\[
 T_{n,x_-}(V_{n,P_0}(x_-))=-\frac12,
 \qquad
 T_{n,x_+}(V_{n,P_0}(x_+))=\frac12.
\]
This contradiction proves that the inclusion is strict.

statements.justification: This is the strengthened headline: it proves the logarithmic lower rate on the same law class while allowing every fixed-point estimator section to be an arbitrary law-independent Borel map.
statements.gap: The full boundary supremum need not be measurable.  The proof therefore lower-bounds and de-Poissonizes a measurable finite packing maximum before invoking finite-maximum domination and monotonicity of outer expectation.
statements.consumer: It supplies the larger-class minimax converse and immediately implies the inherited CTY lower bound by class inclusion.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(q\geq1\) and \(L\geq4\).  For every sufficiently large \(n\), take the family supplied by \(\mathrm{lem:cty\text{-}support\text{-}boundary\text{-}angular\text{-}packing}\).  Write \(M=M_n\), put \(\Delta=c_1a_n\), and let
\[
 C_j=B_2(x_j,w_n)\cap S,
 \qquad 1\leq j\leq M,
\]
be its pairwise disjoint half-disc cells.  The packing lemma gives numbers \(u_{j,0},u_{j,1}\) satisfying
\[
 \mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)=u_{j,\omega_j},
 \qquad |u_{j,1}-u_{j,0}|\geq\Delta.
\]
It also gives \(M_n\geq c_0a_n^{-1/q}\).  By \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rates}\), \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\to0\), and therefore
\[
 M_n\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

Let \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\) be arbitrary.  By \(\mathrm{def:point\text{-}indexed\text{-}distance\text{-}decision\text{-}class}\), it is generated by a law-independent family
\[
 \{T_{n,x}:x\in\mathbb R^2\},
 \qquad
 T_{n,x}:(\mathbb R\times[0,\infty))^n\longrightarrow\mathbb R,
\]
such that each fixed-\(x\) section is Borel measurable and
\[
 \widehat\mu_{n,P}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)
 =T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))
\]
for every admissible \(P\) and every \(x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\).  No map jointly measurable in \((x,v)\) is assumed or used below.

Embed this fixed-sample rule in an experiment whose restrictions to the cells are independent.  Under \(P_\omega\), generate a Poisson random measure on
\[
 \mathbb R\times S\times(0,1)
\]
with intensity \(2n\,P_\omega(dy,dx)\,du\), where \(u\) is an independent uniform mark.  Its total count \(N\) has the \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\) law.  If \(N\geq n\), retain the \(n\) observations having the smallest marks, order them by their marks, form their compressed distance sample at each queried point, and apply the corresponding section \(T_{n,x}\).  If \(N<n\), return zero at every queried point.  Ties have probability zero and may be resolved by any fixed Borel rule.  Denote the resulting pointwise rule by \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}\).  Conditional on \(N=k\geq n\), the retained observations are independent with common law \(P_\omega\), because the marks are independent of the observations and their ordering gives a random permutation independent of the observation values.  The construction uses the fixed family \(\{T_{n,x}\}\), so it is independent of \(\omega\).

Put independent uniform bits \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) on the packing vertices.  Let \(Z_j\) be the complete marked restriction of the Poisson random measure to \(C_j\), and let \(Z_0\) be its restriction to
\[
 S\setminus\bigcup_{j=1}^M C_j.
\]
The marked observation space is standard Borel, as is its space of finite counting measures.  Conditional on the bits, \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) are independent, because restrictions of a Poisson random measure to disjoint Borel sets are independent.  The cellwise locality asserted by \(\mathrm{lem:cty\text{-}support\text{-}boundary\text{-}angular\text{-}packing}\) implies that the law of \(Z_j\) depends only on \(\Omega_j\), whereas the law of \(Z_0\) is independent of all bits.

For each \(j\), let \(S_j\) retain from \(Z_j\) only every point's mark, outcome, and distance from \(x_j\).  A decoder constructed from \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x_j)\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\).  Indeed, the full restrictions outside \(C_j\) reveal the marks, outcomes, and locations of all off-cell points and hence their distances from \(x_j\), while \(S_j\) supplies exactly the marks, outcomes, and distances of the in-cell points.  Sorting the finitely many revealed marks reconstructs the retained ordered compressed sample at \(x_j\).  The fixed section \(T_{n,x_j}\) is Borel measurable by definition.  Thus \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x_j)\), and every Borel threshold of it, is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\).  This argument is separate for each \(j\) and uses no regularity of \(x\mapsto T_{n,x}\).

We next verify the relative-entropy hypothesis of \(\mathrm{lem:coordinatewise\text{-}overlap\text{-}direct\text{-}product}\).  Adjacent packing laws are identical off \(C_j\), their common cell mass is \(m_n\), and every support point at distance less than \(w_n\) from \(x_j\) belongs to \(C_j\).  Let \(\nu_{j,b}\) be the subprobability law of one outcome--distance pair restricted to \(C_j\), under bit value \(b\in\{0,1\}\).  Both subprobabilities have mass \(m_n\).  The corresponding complete one-observation compressed laws have the disjoint-support form
\[
 \nu_{j,b}+\lambda_j,
\]
where \(\lambda_j\) is common to the two bits and is supported on radii at least \(w_n\), while \(\nu_{j,b}\) is supported on radii below \(w_n\), up to null boundaries.  Orient the bits and define
\[
 D_j=\int\log\!\left(\frac{d\nu_{j,0}}{d\nu_{j,1}}\right)d\nu_{j,0}.
\]
The disjoint-support decomposition and factorization of likelihood ratios give
\[
 nD_j
 =\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
 \mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
 \mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}
 \right)
 \leq\alpha\log M.
\]
The finiteness of this divergence supplies the required absolute continuity.  Interchanging the adjacent vertices gives the same assertion in the reverse orientation.

Let \(Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b)\).  Under either bit, the cell count has the common law
\[
 K_j\sim\operatorname{Pois}(2nm_n),
\]
and the independent marks contribute no relative entropy.  Conditional on \(K_j=k\), the compressed cell points are independent with law \(\nu_{j,b}/m_n\).  Since the two subprobabilities have the same mass,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(\nu_{j,0}/m_n,\nu_{j,1}/m_n)
 =\frac{D_j}{m_n}.
\]
Conditioning on the common count and taking expectations yields
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})
 =\mathbb E[K_j]\frac{D_j}{m_n}
 =2nD_j
 \leq2\alpha\log M.
\]
The packing lemma fixes \(0<\alpha<1/8\); hence \(\kappa=2\alpha<1\).

At \(x_j\), decode \(\Omega_j\) by thresholding \(\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x_j)\) at the midpoint of \(u_{j,0}\) and \(u_{j,1}\), with the inequality reversed when \(u_{j,1}<u_{j,0}\).  The exact finite-\(M\) conclusion of \(\mathrm{lem:coordinatewise\text{-}overlap\text{-}direct\text{-}product}\), applied with \(\kappa=2\alpha\), gives
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one coordinate is decoded incorrectly}\}
 \geq\frac12\left[1-\exp\{-M_n^{1-2\alpha}/2\}\right].
\]
Because \(M_n\to\infty\) and \(2\alpha<1\), the right-hand side is \(1/2-o(1)\), with the displayed finite-\(M_n\) expression retained for the next step.

Define the measurable finite-coordinate loss
\[
 L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin,Pois}}
 =\max_{1\leq j\leq M_n}
 \left|
 \widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{Pois}}(x_j)-\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)
 \right|.
\]
It is measurable because it is the maximum of finitely many random variables obtained from Borel fixed-point sections.  If any midpoint decoder errs, then the separation inequality implies
\[
 L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin,Pois}}\geq\frac{\Delta}{2}.
\]
Averaging over the uniform bit prior and using the preceding error bound therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 2^{-M_n}\sum_{\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}}
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}^{\mathrm{Pois}}
 \left[L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin,Pois}}\right]
 &\geq\frac{\Delta}{2}
 \Pr\{\text{at least one decoding error}\}\\
 &\geq\frac{\Delta}{4}
 \left[1-\exp\{-M_n^{1-2\alpha}/2\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sup_\omega
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}^{\mathrm{Pois}}
 \left[L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin,Pois}}\right]
 \geq\frac{\Delta}{4}
 \left[1-\exp\{-M_n^{1-2\alpha}/2\}\right].
\]

We now de-Poissonize this finite maximum, without invoking the measurability of a supremum over the whole boundary.  Define
\[
 L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin}}
 =\max_{1\leq j\leq M_n}
 \left|
 \widehat\mu_{n,P_\omega}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x_j)
 -\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)
 \right|.
\]
This is again measurable.  The packing construction has \(1/4\leq\mu_{P_\omega}\leq3/4\), so on \(\{N<n\}\) the zero default has finite-coordinate loss at most one.  On \(\{N\geq n\}\), the retained observations have law \(P_\omega^{\otimes n}\) and are processed at every \(x_j\) by the original fixed section \(T_{n,x_j}\).  Hence, for every \(\omega\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}^{\mathrm{Pois}}
 \left[L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin,Pois}}\right]
 \leq
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}
 \left[L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin}}\right]
 +\Pr\{\operatorname{Pois}(2n)<n\}.
\]
For \(N\sim\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\), Markov's inequality applied to \(e^{-tN}\), with \(t=\log2\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Pr\{N<n\}
 &\leq e^{tn}\mathbb E[e^{-tN}]\\
 &=\exp\{n\log2+2n(2^{-1}-1)\}\\
 &=\exp\{-n(1-\log2)\}
 =o(a_n).
\end{aligned}
\]
Combining the last three displays, using \(\Delta=c_1a_n\), and then decreasing the positive constant if necessary yields a constant \(c=c(q,L)>0\) such that
\[
 \sup_\omega
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}
 \left[L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin}}\right]
 \geq c a_n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).

For each \(\omega\), the pointwise inequality
\[
 L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin}}
 \leq
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(S)}
 \left|
 \widehat\mu_{n,P_\omega}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)
 -\mu_{P_\omega}(x)
 \right|
\]
holds even if the supremum on the right is not measurable.  By the definition of outer expectation in \(\mathrm{def:point\text{-}indexed\text{-}distance\text{-}risk}\), every measurable majorant of the right-hand side also majorizes the measurable variable on the left.  Therefore
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}
 \left[L_{n,\omega}^{\mathrm{fin}}\right]
 \leq
 \mathbb E_{P_\omega}^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(S)}
 \left|
 \widehat\mu_{n,P_\omega}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)
 -\mu_{P_\omega}(x)
 \right|
 \right].
\]
This is the only passage from the finite packing points to the whole boundary, and it requires no measurability of the latter supremum.

The packing lemma explicitly verifies independent sampling, compact support, density positivity, rectifiable boundary, H\"older regression, and continuous conditional variance for every \(P_\omega\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).  The supremum over the full class is therefore no smaller than the supremum over this finite family.  Since the point-indexed rule was arbitrary, the last two inequalities imply
\[
 R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}
 =\inf_{\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\in\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}
 \left|
 \widehat\mu_{n,P}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)-\mu_P(x)
 \right|
 \right]
 \geq c a_n
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Dividing by \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) and taking lower limits proves the displayed conclusion with \(c_{\mathrm{PI}}=c\).  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:common\text{-}map\text{-}strict\text{-}in\text{-}point\text{-}indexed}\) shows that this sectionwise-Borel point-indexed class strictly contains the inherited common-map class.  No Assumption~2 upper theorem and no full-class achievability statement enter the argument.

statements.statement: The collection of all closed Euclidean balls in \(\mathbb R^2\) is a VC class with VC index at most four.  Hence the fixed Euclidean metric and uniform kernel in \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}class}\) satisfy the actual VC alternative in CTY Assumption~2(iii), uniformly over every member law.

statements.proof_tex:
Define the lifted feature vector
\[
 \Phi(z)=(1,z_1,z_2,\lVert z\rVert_2^2)\in\mathbb R^4.
\]
For a center \(c\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\geq0\), put
\[
 a_{c,r}=(\lVert c\rVert_2^2-r^2,-2c_1,-2c_2,1).
\]
Then the algebraic identity
\[
 \lVert z-c\rVert_2^2-r^2=a_{c,r}^{\top}\Phi(z)
\]
shows that
\[
 z\in B_2(c,r)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a_{c,r}^{\top}\Phi(z)\leq0.
\]

We prove directly that no four points can be shattered.  Take arbitrary \(z_1,\ldots,z_4\in\mathbb R^2\) and write \(v_i=\Phi(z_i)\).  First suppose that the four vectors are linearly dependent.  Choose real numbers \(\lambda_i\), not all zero, such that
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^4\lambda_i v_i=0.
\]
The first coordinate of every \(v_i\) is one, so \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\); hence the nonzero coefficients include both signs.  Label \(z_i\) inside when \(\lambda_i>0\) and outside when \(\lambda_i<0\), assigning arbitrary labels to zero coefficients.  If a closed ball realized this labeling, then
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^4\lambda_i a_{c,r}^{\top}v_i<0:
\]
the positive-coefficient terms are nonpositive, while every negative coefficient multiplies a strictly positive outside-ball value.  This contradicts
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^4\lambda_i a_{c,r}^{\top}v_i
 =a_{c,r}^{\top}\sum_{i=1}^4\lambda_i v_i=0.
\]

It remains to consider the linearly independent case.  With \(e_4=(0,0,0,1)\), there are unique coefficients \(\lambda_i\) satisfying
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^4\lambda_i v_i=e_4.
\]
Again the first coordinate gives \(\sum_i\lambda_i=0\), so both signs occur.  Use the same sign labeling.  Any realizing ball would again make the weighted sum strictly negative, but the defining fourth coordinate of \(a_{c,r}\) gives
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^4\lambda_i a_{c,r}^{\top}v_i
 =a_{c,r}^{\top}e_4=1,
\]
a contradiction.  Thus no set of four planar points is shattered by closed Euclidean balls.  Their VC dimension is at most three, and therefore their VC index is at most four.  Restriction of the balls to any support \(\mathcal X_P\) cannot increase the index.  Since the fixed Euclidean metric and \(K_\square(u)=\mathbf 1\{|u|\leq1\}\) generate precisely these restricted radius sublevel sets, the VC clause in \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}class}\) follows uniformly over every member law.

If \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), then for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[|Y(t)-\mu_{t,P}(X)|^{2+\nu}\mid X\right]
 \leq 2^{2+\nu}L
\]
almost surely.  Thus every centered residual moment invoked by the local-polynomial expansion follows from, and is not substituted for, CTY's raw conditional-moment envelope.

statements.proof_tex:
Put \(r=2+\nu\geq4\).  Conditional Jensen gives
\[
 |\mu_{t,P}(X)|^r
 =|\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X]|^r
 \leq\mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|^r\mid X].
\]
The elementary convexity inequality \(|a-b|^r\leq2^{r-1}(|a|^r+|b|^r)\) therefore yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_P[|Y(t)-\mu_{t,P}(X)|^r\mid X]
 &\leq2^{r-1}\{\mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|^r\mid X]+|\mu_{t,P}(X)|^r\}\\
 &\leq2^r\mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|^r\mid X]
 \leq2^{2+\nu}L,
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last inequality is clause \(\mathrm{(v)}\) of \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}class}\).  This proves the claim.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq1\) and every \(\nu\geq2\), there is a finite \(L_0=L_0(p)\geq48\) such that, for every \(L\geq L_0\) and all sufficiently small \(\Delta>0\), the class \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) contains a hypercube \(\{P_\omega:\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\}\) with the common known geometry
\[
 \mathcal X=[-3,3]^2,
 \quad \mathcal A_1=[-1,1]\times[0,2],
 \quad \mathcal A_0=\mathcal X\setminus\mathcal A_1,
 \quad \mathcal B=\partial\mathcal A_1,
\]
Euclidean distance, and \(K_\square\).  Writing \(q=p+1\), the family has \(M\geq c\Delta^{-1/q}\) disjoint disks \(S_j=B_2(x_j,w)\), with \(x_j\) on the middle of the bottom edge, \(w=A\Delta^{1/q}\), and the following properties:

\(\mathrm{(a)}\) every member satisfies every clause of \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}class}\), including density normalization and envelopes, the raw conditional moment bound, the corner geometry, local kernel mass, Euclidean-ball VC condition, radial Hausdorff positivity, and the uniform Gram eigenvalue bound;

\(\mathrm{(b)}\) the cell label probabilities are bit-independent and equal,
\[
 P_\omega(X\in S_j)=\rho={\pi w^2\over36};
\]
the law restricted to \(S_j\) depends only on \(\omega_j\), and the law outside \(\bigcup_jS_j\) is bit-independent;

\(\mathrm{(c)}\) if \(\omega^{(j)}\) differs only in coordinate \(j\), then
\[
 |\tau_{P_\omega}(x_j)-\tau_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)|=\Delta;
\]

\(\mathrm{(d)}\) conditional on \(X\in S_j\), the adjacent one-observation signed-distance laws \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) of \((Y,D^{\pm}_{P,x_j})\) have the same signed-radius marginal, agree outside \(0<D^{\pm}_{P,x_j}<2C\Delta\), and obey, in both orientations,
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq C_0{\Delta^4\over w^2}.
\]
All constants are independent of \(M\), \(\omega\), \(\Delta\), and \(n\).
statements.justification: This is the same-class least-favorable family with fixed support, fixed known assignment, and fixed interior boundary.
statements.gap: It verifies every CTY A1/A2 and Theorem~2 condition, including corners, VC complexity, Gram stability, and raw moments.
statements.consumer: The A1/A2 point-indexed converse uses its local KL, target separation, equal cell masses, and bit locality.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(q=p+1\).  Fix smooth functions \(\phi,\eta:[0,\infty)\to[0,1]\) such that \(\phi=1\) near zero, \(\phi=0\) on \([1,\infty)\), all transition endpoints are flat, \(\eta(u)=0\) for \(u\leq1\), and \(\eta(u)=1\) for \(u\geq2\).  The radial function may be chosen as a smooth function of squared radius, so its pullback to \(\mathbb R^2\) is smooth at the origin.  Choose constants in the order: a small slope \(a>0\), a large cutoff constant \(C\), and a large smoothness constant \(A\).  Put
\[
 w=A\Delta^{1/q}.
\]
Place \(x_j=(s_j,0)\) on \([-1/2,1/2]\times\{0\}\) with separation at least \(4w\).  Elementary interval packing gives
\[
 M\asymp w^{-1}\geq c\Delta^{-1/q},
\]
and the disks \(S_j=B_2(x_j,w)\) are disjoint, contained in \(\mathcal X=[-3,3]^2\), and avoid the corners of \(\mathcal B=\partial([-1,1]\times[0,2])\).

For \(r>0\), define
\[
 b_{\Delta,w}(r)={2\Delta\over ar}\phi(r/w)\eta(r/(C\Delta)),
 \qquad b_{\Delta,w}(0)=0.
\]
For \(x\in S_j\), write \(x-x_j=r_j(\cos\alpha_j,\sin\alpha_j)\), and interpret every summand below as zero outside its disk.  For \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), let
\[
 f_\omega(x)={1\over36}\left[1+\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_jb_{\Delta,w}(r_j)\cos\alpha_j\right],
\]
\[
 \mu_{0,\omega}(x)={1\over2},
 \qquad
 \mu_{1,\omega}(x)={1\over2}+ax_1-\Delta\sum_{j=1}^M\omega_j\phi(r_j/w).
\]
Conditional on \(X=x\), take \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) conditionally independent Bernoulli variables with these respective success probabilities.  Treatment and observation obey the fixed deterministic assignment and consistency equations in the class definition.

We verify the law-class clauses one by one.  The density perturbation vanishes on \(r\leq C\Delta\) and smoothly before \(r=w\), so the apparent factor \(1/r\) creates no singularity and \(f_\omega\) is continuous on the square.  Whenever it is nonzero,
\[
 |b_{\Delta,w}(r)|\leq {2\over aC}.
\]
Choose \(C\) so large that this is at most \(1/4\).  Because the disks are disjoint,
\[
 {1\over48}\leq f_\omega(x)\leq {5\over144}.
\]
Moreover, polar integration on every full disk gives
\[
 \int_0^w b_{\Delta,w}(r)r\,dr\int_0^{2\pi}\cos\alpha\,d\alpha=0.
\]
Since the square has area \(36\), \(\int_{\mathcal X}f_\omega=1\).  Thus the density is normalized, positive on the entire fixed support, continuous, and satisfies the required envelope once \(L_0\geq48\).

For every derivative order \(0\leq k\leq q\), scaling and disjointness give
\[
 \left\|D^k\left[\Delta\sum_j\omega_j\phi(\lVert\,\cdot-x_j\rVert_2/w)\right]\right\|_\infty
 \leq C_k\Delta w^{-k}=C_kA^{-k}\Delta^{1-k/q}.
\]
At \(k=q\) the right side is \(C_qA^{-q}\), and for \(k<q\) it tends to zero.  Choosing \(A\) large verifies both the derivative suprema through order \(p\) and the Lipschitz bounds for every such derivative.  The formula extends smoothly past the support because all disks are strictly interior and the affine term is global.  Taking \(a\) and then \(\Delta\) small puts both Bernoulli probabilities in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Hence their conditional variances lie in \([3/16,1/4]\), their raw conditional \((2+\nu)\)-moments are at most one for every \(\nu\geq2\), and all the variance, moment, and regression clauses hold.  Independent replication gives the required sampling condition for every \(n\).

The assignment rectangle has perimeter eight and is at Euclidean distance at least one from the support boundary.  Its boundary is therefore a compact positive-length rectifiable curve in the support interior.  At a smooth edge or a corner and for all sufficiently small \(h\), each arm contains a circular sector centered at the boundary point with opening angle at least \(\pi/2\).  Since the kernel equals one on the unit ball, scaling such a sector by \(h^{-1}\) gives
\[
 {1\over h^2}\int_{\mathcal A_t}K_\square(\{(2t-1)\lVert z-x\rVert_2\}/h)\,dz\geq {\pi\over8}.
\]
The corresponding radius-\(s\) arc has length between \((\pi/2)s\) and \(2\pi s\); multiplication by the density envelope proves that the Hausdorff denominator is positive and finite at edges and corners alike.

For the Gram condition, use polar coordinates in one of those sectors.  For a coefficient vector \(v\in\mathbb R^{p+1}\) and the sign \(\epsilon_t=2t-1\), the density lower bound gives
\[
 v^\top\Psi_{t,P_\omega,x}(h)v
 \geq c\int_0^1\{v^\top r_p(\epsilon_tu)\}^2u\,du.
\]
The integral is strictly positive for every nonzero \(v\), because a nonzero polynomial cannot vanish on an interval.  It is continuous on the unit sphere, which is compact, so its minimum there is positive.  This yields a lower eigenvalue depending only on \(p\) and the fixed density and sector constants.  Enlarging \(L_0(p)\) verifies the displayed uniform Gram bound.  Finally, the Euclidean-ball VC proof in \(\mathrm{lem:euclidean\text{-}balls\text{-}vc}\) applies to this fixed metric, including after restriction to the square.  Thus every A1/A2 and Theorem~2 clause holds for every vertex.

We next establish locality and target separation.  Each disk perturbation integrates to zero, so
\[
 P_\omega(X\in S_j)={|S_j|\over36}={\pi w^2\over36}=\rho
\]
for every \(j\) and \(\omega\).  Disjoint supports show that the joint law restricted to \(S_j\) depends only on \(\omega_j\), while all perturbations vanish outside their union.  At \(x_j\),
\[
 \tau_{P_\omega}(x_j)=\mu_{1,\omega}(x_j)-\mu_{0,\omega}(x_j)=as_j-\Delta\omega_j,
\]
so adjacent target values differ by exactly \(\Delta\).

It remains to calculate the compressed information.  Inside \(S_j\), positive signed radius is the upper semicircle \(0\leq\alpha\leq\pi\) and negative signed radius is the lower semicircle.  The identities
\[
 \int_0^\pi\cos\alpha\,d\alpha=0,
 \qquad
 \int_0^\pi\cos^2\alpha\,d\alpha={\pi\over2}
\]
show that both signed-radius marginals are bit-independent.  Conditional on the disk, their density is \(r/w^2\) on each of \((0,w)\) and \((-w,0)\).  On the control half, the observed Bernoulli mean is always \(1/2\).  On the treatment half, angular averaging gives, for \(r>0\),
\[
 q_{0,j}(r)={1\over2}+as_j,
\]
and
\[
 q_{1,j}(r)-q_{0,j}(r)
 =-\Delta\phi(r/w)+{ar\over2}b_{\Delta,w}(r)
 =-\Delta\phi(r/w)\{1-\eta(r/(C\Delta))\}.
\]
Thus the complete conditional outcome--signed-distance laws agree unless \(0<r<2C\Delta\).  Their Bernoulli probabilities remain in \([1/4,3/4]\), so in either KL orientation
\[
 \operatorname{kl}(u,v)\leq { (u-v)^2\over v(1-v)}\leq C_1\Delta^2.
\]
Disintegration over the common signed-radius marginal yields
\[
 \operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})
 \leq C_1\Delta^2\int_0^{2C\Delta}{r\over w^2}\,dr
 \leq C_0{\Delta^4\over w^2},
\]
and reversing the adjacent vertices gives the same bound.  This proves every assertion.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq1\) and every \(\nu\geq2\), there is a finite \(L_0=L_0(p)\) such that, for every \(L\geq L_0\), there is \(c=c(p,\nu,L)>0\) satisfying
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}\left({n\over\log n}\right)^{1/4}R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\geq c.
\]
The conclusion holds for arbitrary law-independent known-geometry point-indexed families with Borel fixed sections, under outer expectation and without joint regularity in the boundary index.  The hard subclass has one fixed support, one fixed known assignment rectangle, and one fixed known interior treatment boundary.
statements.justification: This proves the logarithmic converse on the exact regular A1/A2 class for a decision class larger than CTY's estimator architecture.
statements.gap: The good-count event and conditional direct-product step repair the missing fixed-sample coupling argument.
statements.consumer: It supplies the lower half of the matched frontier and the lower endpoint of the fourth-moment bracket.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\geq1\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq L_0(p)\), and write \(q=p+1\).  Choose
\[
 \Delta_n=\gamma a_n=\gamma\left({\log n\over n}\right)^{1/4},
 \qquad w_n=A\Delta_n^{1/q},
\]
where \(\gamma>0\) will be fixed sufficiently small.  Apply \(\mathrm{lem:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}rectangle\text{-}angular\text{-}hypercube}\).  It gives \(M=M_n\asymp w_n^{-1}\to\infty\), common cell probability \(\rho_n=\pi w_n^2/36\), and adjacent conditional cell divergence at most \(C_0\Delta_n^4/w_n^2\).

Put independent uniform bits \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) on the vertices.  For the exactly \(n\) independent observations, let \(J_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,M\}\) record whether \(X_i\) lies outside all disks or in disk \(S_j\).  The entire label vector has a distribution independent of the bits, by the common cell-mass and locality properties.  Conditional on the labels, let \(N_j=\sum_i\mathbf 1\{J_i=j\}\).  The observations in the labeled blocks are independent; block \(j\) depends only on \(\Omega_j\), and block zero is bit-independent.

We verify the simultaneous good-count step before applying any testing inequality.  Marginally, \(N_j\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,\rho_n)\).  The multiplicative Chernoff inequality at factor two gives
\[
 \Pr\{N_j>2n\rho_n\}\leq(e/4)^{n\rho_n}\leq\exp(-n\rho_n/3).
\]
Consequently, for
\[
 G_n=\left\{\max_{1\leq j\leq M_n}N_j\leq2n\rho_n\right\},
\]
the union bound yields
\[
 \Pr(G_n^c)\leq M_n\exp(-n\rho_n/3).
\]
Now
\[
 n\rho_n\asymp n\Delta_n^{2/q}
 =n^{1-1/(2q)}(\log n)^{1/(2q)},
 \qquad \log M_n=O(\log n).
\]
Since \(q\geq2\), \(n\rho_n/\log M_n\to\infty\), and hence \(\Pr(G_n)\to1\).

Fix a realization of the labels in \(G_n\).  For decoder \(j\), let \(S_j\) be its own cell's ordered outcome--signed-distance block, and reveal the complete raw blocks \(Z_{-j}\) and \(Z_0\) outside cell \(j\).  These revealed blocks reconstruct every off-cell signed distance to \(x_j\), while \(S_j\) supplies the in-cell part.  Therefore the fixed Borel section \(T_{n,G,x_j}\), and its midpoint bit decoder, are measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\).  This is a coordinatewise statement and uses no joint regularity in \(x\).

Conditional tensorization and the hard-family KL calculation give, in both orientations,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{KL}\{\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=0,J_{1:n}),
                      \mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=1,J_{1:n})\}
 &\leq N_jC_0{\Delta_n^4\over w_n^2}\\
 &\leq2n\rho_nC_0{\Delta_n^4\over w_n^2}
 =C_1n\Delta_n^4.
\end{aligned}
\]
Because
\[
 C_1n\Delta_n^4=C_1\gamma^4\log n,
 \qquad
 \log M_n={1\over4q}\log n+O(\log\log n),
\]
we may choose \(\gamma\) so small that, for one fixed \(\kappa<1\), the last divergence is at most \(\kappa\log M_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:coordinatewise\text{-}overlap\text{-}direct\text{-}product}\) conditionally on every label realization in \(G_n\).  It yields
\[
 \Pr\{\text{some coordinate decoder errs}\mid J_{1:n}\}
 \geq {1\over2}\left[1-\exp\{-M_n^{1-\kappa}/2\}\right].
\]
Averaging over the labels and using \(\Pr(G_n)\to1\) and \(M_n\to\infty\) gives
\[
 2^{-M_n}\sum_\omega P_\omega\{\text{some decoder errs}\}\geq {1\over2}-o(1).
\]

At \(x_j\), decode by selecting the nearer of the two target values.  If this decoder errs, then
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq M_n}|\widehat\tau_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)-\tau_{P_\omega}(x_j)|\geq{\Delta_n\over2}.
\]
The finite maximum is measurable because every fixed-point section is Borel.  It is pointwise no larger than the possibly nonmeasurable full boundary supremum.  Monotonicity in the definition of outer expectation therefore gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right]
 \geq {\Delta_n\over2}\left({1\over2}-o(1)\right).
\]
The rule was arbitrary.  Taking its infimum, dividing by \(a_n\), and taking the lower limit proves the theorem with a positive constant proportional to \(\gamma\).

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq1\), every \(\nu\geq2\), and every \(L\geq4\), the explicit stabilized estimator in \(\mathrm{def:cty\text{-}stabilized\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}estimator}\), with bandwidth \(h_n=b_{n,\nu}\), satisfies for all sufficiently large \(n\)
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
 |\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq Cb_{n,\nu}.
\]
This expected outer-risk statement is a derived corollary of CTY's first-order bias theorem and the expected maximal-inequality displays in its supplement; it is not asserted to be the verbatim statement of CTY Theorem~4(ii).
statements.justification: It turns CTY's source-backed bias and expected empirical-process bounds into a usable outer-expected risk bound for one explicit estimator.
statements.gap: CTY prints a probability-order theorem; this derived corollary proves the stronger expectation statement needed for minimax risk.
statements.consumer: It is the upper half of the matched frontier and supplies the optimized fourth-moment endpoint rate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) and a bandwidth \(h\leq L^{-1}\).  Let \(\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\) be the population local-polynomial coefficient and \(\widehat O_{t,x}(h)\) the centered empirical score at that coefficient.  Define the global good-Gram event
\[
 \mathcal G_h=\left\{
 \sup_{t\in\{0,1\},\,x\in\mathcal B_P}
 \lVert\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)-\Psi_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert
 \leq(2L)^{-1}
 \right\}.
\]
Clause \(\mathrm{(viii)}\) of the class definition and Weyl's eigenvalue inequality give, on \(\mathcal G_h\),
\[
 \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h))
 \geq\lambda_{\min}(\Psi_{t,P,x}(h))
 -\lVert\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)-\Psi_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert
 \geq(2L)^{-1}.
\]
Thus stabilization does not activate on \(\mathcal G_h\), and the empirical and population normal equations imply
\[
 \lVert\widehat\beta_{t,x}(h)-\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert
 \leq2L\lVert\widehat O_{t,x}(h)\rVert.
\]

The cited first-order bias lemma gives, uniformly in \(P\) and \(x\),
\[
 \left|e_1^\top\{\beta^*_{1,P,x}(h)-\beta^*_{0,P,x}(h)\}-\tau_P(x)\right|\leq Ch.
\]
Because the order-zero part of the regression envelope gives \(|\mu_{t,P}(x)|\leq L\), the true contrast belongs to \([-2L,2L]\).  Projection onto that interval is one-Lipschitz.  Consequently, on \(\mathcal G_h\),
\[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
 |\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \leq Ch+C\sup_{t,x}\lVert\widehat O_{t,x}(h)\rVert.
\]
On \(\mathcal G_h^c\), clipping bounds the loss by \(4L\).  Markov's inequality and the cited expected Gram bound give
\[
 P(\mathcal G_h^c)
 \leq2L\mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{t,x}\lVert\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)-\Psi_{t,P,x}(h)\rVert
 \right]
 \leq C\sqrt{{\log(1/h)\over nh^2}}.
\]
The class uses CTY's raw moment envelope; the centered moment required for \(\widehat O\) follows explicitly from \(\mathrm{lem:cty\text{-}raw\text{-}to\text{-}centered\text{-}moment}\).  Combining the preceding bounds with \(\mathrm{lem:cty\text{-}expected\text{-}local\text{-}polynomial\text{-}maximal\text{-}bounds}\) yields
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_x|\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right]
 \leq C\left\{
 h+\sqrt{{\log(1/h)\over nh^2}}
 +{\log(1/h)\over n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h^2}
 \right\}.
\]

For completeness, the outer expectation is not hiding a measurability gap for this particular rule.  For a fixed known geometry, \((x,(Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n)\mapsto D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\) is Borel, as are the finite sums, eigenvalue threshold, matrix inverse on the nonsingular set, and projection defining the stabilized estimator.  The target \(\tau_P\) is continuous.  Thus the loss is jointly Borel on the compact boundary times the raw sample space.  Its boundary supremum is upper semianalytic, hence universally measurable, and its completed expectation equals its outer expectation.  This argument is used only for the explicit upper-bound witness, not for arbitrary members of \(\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}\).

Now take \(h=h_n=b_{n,\nu}\).  Then \(h_n\to0\) and
\[
 {n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h_n^2\over\log(1/h_n)}\to\infty,
\]
because \(h_n\) is at least the cube-root term in its definition.  Also \(h_n\geq a_n\), so the square-root stochastic term is \(O(a_n)\), and
\[
 h_n\geq\left\{{\log n\over n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}}\right\}^{1/3}
\]
makes the heavy-tail term no larger than the same cube-root rate.  Since \(\log(1/h_n)\asymp\log n\), the last risk display is \(O(b_{n,\nu})\), as claimed.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq1\) and every \(\nu>2\), there is a finite \(L_0=L_0(p)\) such that, for every \(L\geq L_0\), there are \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) with
\[
 c\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n}
 \leq\limsup_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n}\leq C.
\]
Thus the outer-expected minimax frontier over the same exact uniformized CTY Assumptions~1--2 class is \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\).  The upper bound is attained by the explicit stabilized signed-distance local-polynomial estimator, while the lower bound holds over the larger class of all law-independent known-geometry point-indexed Borel sections.
statements.justification: For conditional moments strictly above fourth order, the lower and explicit upper rates coincide on exactly one class and risk.
statements.gap: This removes the support-boundary versus interior-assignment-boundary mismatch for the regular CTY theory.
statements.consumer: This is the lead statistical frontier theorem for the A1/A2 family.
statements.proof_tex:
The converse \(\mathrm{thm:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}point\text{-}indexed\text{-}log\text{-}converse}\) gives the positive lower limit.  The explicit stabilized estimator is one member of \(\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}\), so the minimax risk is no larger than its worst-law outer risk.  The upper proposition therefore gives
\[
 R_n^{12,\pm}(p,\nu,L)\leq Cb_{n,\nu}.
\]
When \(\nu>2\),
\[
 {1+\nu\over3(2+\nu)}>{1\over4},
\]
and hence
\[
 \left\{{\log n\over n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}}\right\}^{1/3}=o(a_n).
\]
It follows that \(b_{n,\nu}/a_n\to1\).  Dividing the upper inequality by \(a_n\), taking the upper limit, and combining it with the converse proves the matched display.

statements.statement:
For every integer \(p\geq1\), there is a finite \(L_0=L_0(p)\) such that, for every \(L\geq L_0\), there are constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\) satisfying, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c\left({\log n\over n}\right)^{1/4}
 \leq R^{12,\pm}_n(p,2,L)
 \leq Cn^{-1/4}(\log n)^{1/3}.
\]
Thus the fourth-moment endpoint has a proved two-sided bracket under exactly the same class; the residual logarithmic gap is not claimed to be tight.
statements.justification: It records the best honest optimized upper rate at the fourth-moment endpoint instead of claiming an unsupported match.
statements.gap: The source-backed heavy-tail term leaves a residual factor of \(\log^{1/12}n\) between the upper and lower rates.
statements.consumer: Readers with only fourth conditional moments receive an explicit two-sided rate bracket.
statements.proof_tex:
The lower inequality is the finite-\(n\) consequence of \(\mathrm{thm:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}point\text{-}indexed\text{-}log\text{-}converse}\), after decreasing its positive constant.  At \(\nu=2\),
\[
 b_{n,2}=\left({\log n\over n}\right)^{1/4}
 +\left({\log n\over n^{3/4}}\right)^{1/3}
 =a_n+n^{-1/4}(\log n)^{1/3}.
\]
The second summand dominates the first for all large \(n\).  Applying \(\mathrm{prop:cty\text{-}a1\text{-}a2\text{-}expected\text{-}outer\text{-}upper}\) to the explicit minimax witness gives the stated upper inequality.  No equality of the two logarithmic exponents follows from these assumptions.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The regression \(\mu_P\) lies in \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\), and the continuous conditional variance satisfies \(L^{-1}\leq\sigma_P^2(x)\leq L\).  At each boundary point the estimator observes only \(V_{n,P}(x)\).  In the strengthened class it may apply an arbitrary point-specific section \(T_{n,x}\), provided every fixed section is Borel measurable and the family is selected independently of \(P\); no joint regularity in \(x\) is required.  The inherited CTY class restricts all sections to one common map.
sampling_model.design: Nonparametric regression with a bivariate random-design covariate \(X\), compact support \(\mathcal X_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), and rectifiable support boundary; the target is the single observed-outcome regression \(\mu_P\) restricted to that boundary.
sampling_model.units: The observations \((Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independently and identically distributed under every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).
sampling_model.treatment: This field is not applicable to the observed-outcome regression model; the estimand is \(\mu_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x]\).
sampling_model.overlap: The score has a continuous Lebesgue density on its compact support satisfying \(L^{-1}\leq f_P(x)\leq L\).

estimand_functional:
The note has two distinct, non-substitutable statistical functionals.  First, for \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), the causal target is the boundary treatment-effect curve \(\tau_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\).  Under CTY Theorem~1 it equals the difference of the two one-sided signed-distance conditional-mean limits.  The estimator observes \(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n)\), may use the known geometry \(G_P\), and belongs to the law-independent sectionwise-Borel class \(\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}\).  Its explicit outer-expectation minimax functional is
\[
 R_n^{12,\pm}(p,\nu,L)=\inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T_n^{12,\pm}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|\right].
\]
For \(q=p+1\geq2\), this risk is of exact order \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) when \(\nu>2\), with the stabilized degree-\(p\) signed-distance local-polynomial rule as an explicit upper witness; at \(\nu=2\) the proved upper rate is \(n^{-1/4}(\log n)^{1/3}\).

Second, and unchanged from the accepted checkpoint, for each \(x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) the observed input is \(V_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n)\).  The enlarged point-indexed class \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\) consists of all law-independent families \(\{T_{n,x}:x\in\mathbb R^2\}\) whose fixed-\(x\) sections are Borel and whose output is \(T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))\).  Its outer-expectation risk is \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\).  The preserved theorem proves \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) on the full \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), and strict inclusion yields the inherited CTY common-map converse.  No full-\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper theorem is claimed.
target_estimand: Lead target: \(\tau_P(\cdot)=\mathbb E_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=\cdot]\big|_{\mathcal B_P}\) on the exact uniformized CTY Assumptions~1--2 class, identified by the signed-distance limits in CTY Theorem~1.  Complementary preserved target: \(\mu_P(\cdot)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=\cdot]\big|_{\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\).

tldr: For arbitrary law-independent point-indexed distance families \(\{T_{n,x}\}\) whose fixed-point sections are Borel measurable, a decision class strictly larger than the inherited Cattaneo--Titiunik--Yu one-common-map class, the outer-expectation minimax risk satisfies \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\).  The proof works with a measurable finite packing maximum and therefore needs no joint regularity in \(x\).  Since \(\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\subsetneq\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\), the CTY common-map logarithmic converse follows by inclusion and resolves their printed conjecture in the stated regime \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(q\geq1\), and \(L\geq4\).  No Assumption~2 result, full-\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}\) upper bound, or matched two-sided frontier is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu, Theorem~6, gives an \(n^{-1/4}\) lower rate on \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), while its discussion conjectures that the logarithmic uniform penalty is unavoidable.  The missing step is a same-law-class construction producing many hard boundary alternatives.  The strengthened question asks whether the logarithm remains necessary even after their one-common-map restriction is relaxed to arbitrary law-independent point-indexed families with only fixed-section Borel measurability.  Their uniform upper theorem imposes the additional geometric condition in Assumption~2 and hence does not furnish a full-class upper bound under rectifiability alone.
project_justification.niche: Each queried boundary point still receives only its outcome--distance compression, but its Borel decision section \(T_{n,x}\) may depend arbitrarily on \(x\).  A local angular perturbation of the score density compensates a regression bump in the radial outcome law except on radii of order \(a_n\), while disjoint boundary cells turn uniform loss into a simultaneous decentralized testing problem whose decoders may differ by coordinate.
project_justification.fill: The note constructs a hypercube of laws on the square \([-1/2,1/2]^2\), verifies all four defining conditions of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), exposes cellwise bit locality and common cell mass, and proves adjacent compressed Kullback--Leibler divergence at most \(\alpha\log M_n\).  A marked-Poisson cell decomposition and the coordinatewise overlap direct-product lemma lower-bound a measurable finite packing maximum.  De-Poissonization is performed for that finite maximum, which is then bounded by the full boundary supremum using outer expectation.  This proves \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) for the sectionwise-Borel point-indexed class; the inherited common-map theorem follows by inclusion.

related_work: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu (2026), Theorem~6, is the direct comparator: it studies the same nonparametric law class and inherited one-common-map coordinatewise distance architecture and proves an \(n^{-1/4}\) lower rate.  The present angular packing proves the sharper \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\) converse over a strictly larger class of arbitrary law-independent point-indexed families with Borel fixed sections.  The CTY common-map conclusion follows by class inclusion, resolving the logarithmic lower-bound conjecture printed in their discussion in the stated regime \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(q\geq1\), and \(L\geq4\).  Their published uniform upper result applies under the additional geometric condition in Assumption~2; it is not an upper bound over the entire rectifiable-boundary class.  The multiple-coordinate step is proved internally by the coordinatewise overlap direct-product lemma.
interpretation: The logarithm is an information-loss phenomenon for simultaneous boundary recovery from coordinatewise outcome--distance samples, not an artifact of forcing the same estimator map at every point.  Many disjoint angular perturbations remain individually hard after radial compression, and the direct-product argument permits a different Borel decoder at every packed coordinate.  The proof requires no measurability of the arbitrary full boundary supremum: it derives the lower bound for a measurable finite maximum and passes to the full supremum by monotonicity of outer expectation.  The inherited CTY common-map result is a corollary.  Minor envelope-normalization remark: \(1=\int_{\mathcal X_P}f_P\geq|\mathcal X_P|/L\) implies \(|\mathcal X_P|\leq L\), so using support \([-1,1]^2\) requires \(L\geq4\); this is only the normalization built into the CTY density envelope.
technical_internal_limitation: The result is a full-\(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) converse over the larger sectionwise-Borel point-indexed distance class, not a full-class two-sided frontier.  Rectifiability in the displayed class does not supply the additional uniform Gram or geometric condition used by the published upper theory, so that result remains confined to its Assumption~2 subclass.  Because arbitrary point-indexed families need not be jointly measurable in \(x\), the risk uses outer expectation.  The proof avoids this measurability issue by applying the marked-Poisson decomposition, the exact finite-\(M\) direct-product bound with \(\kappa=2\alpha<1\), and de-Poissonization only to the finite packing maximum.
honest_scope: The headline contribution is the lower bound \(R_n^{\mathrm{PI}}\gtrsim(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) on the exact \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) law class for arbitrary law-independent point-indexed coordinatewise distance rules with Borel fixed sections and no regularity in \(x\).  Because the inherited common-map class is a strict subset, the CTY lower-bound conjecture follows as a corollary in the stated regime \(q\in\mathbb N\), \(q\geq1\), and \(L\geq4\).  No exact asymptotic constant, Assumption~2 theorem, matching upper bound over all of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\), or matched two-sided frontier is claimed.
